doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Hoagy Carmichael and Phil Harris at the Thunderbird party in Palm Springs
summary: Haggart and Sutton tell of Hoagy on piano and Phil Harris falling off the drums at a Palm Springs party.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And you were in Palm Springs right after that, remember?
That was the party at The Thunderbird.
Right. That was a football players birthday party, wasn’t it? Remember that?
Well Hoagy and Phil Harris were there.
That’s right. I remember that. We got Hoagy on the piano.

As soon as we walked in the place, these women members of the Thunderbird Club said, “Now don’t let Hoagy and Phil sit in tonight.” The first thing they said. We were just walking in the place in the afternoon. They were all ready for us. Because they were on the bad list, see? Hoagy and Phil did some naughty things in front of the whole membership. The women objected, you see.
But they ended up playing anyhow?
Then came in anyhow, and sat in.
Hoagy, on the piano, with Phil Harris sitting in on drums.
And he went over backwards, didn’t he?
Yeah, he got off the stand and fell right down, smack, on the table. Crashing down on one of the tables in front of the bandstand.
Having a few tastes that night.
He got his foot caught in a wire, you know, a microphone wire. And he went crashing down.
It broke up the party. Don Hudson. Was that the football player?
I don’t remember the football player.
